name: Example: Finding the Interval of Convergence of a Given Power Series
problem:
Find the interval of convergence for the series

$$
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{x^{n}}{3^n\sqrt{n}}=\dfrac{x}{3}+\frac{x^2}{3^2\cdot \sqrt{2}}+\frac{x^3}{3^3\cdot \sqrt{3}}+\frac{x^4}{3^4\cdot 2}+\cdots \,.
$$
worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test, we define $a_n=  \dfrac{x^{n}}{3^n\sqrt{n}}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to\infty\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{x}^{n+1}}{{3}^{n+1}\sqrt{n+1}}\cdot \frac{{3}^{n}\sqrt{n}}{{x}^{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{\sqrt{n}x}{3\sqrt{n+1}}| \\  & =\frac{|x|}{3}{lim}_{n\to \infty }(\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\sqrt{n+1}}) \\  & =\frac{|x|}{3}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{|x|}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L <    1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied for 

$$
\dfrac{|x|}{3}<   1
$$

which gives

$$
|x| < 3.
$$

 

So, the radius of convergence is $3,$ and the series converges for any $x$ that lies in the open interval $(-3,3).$

The ratio test gives no conclusion about the convergence of the series when $L=1.$ So, when $|x|=3,$ we do not know if the series converges. This means that the endpoints $x=-3$ and $x=3$ need to be investigated separately using another test for convergence.

- When $x=3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{n}}{{3}^{n}\sqrt{n}} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{3}^{n}}{{3}^{n}\sqrt{n}} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \\  & =1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{4}}+⋯\,,\end{aligned}
$$

which is divergent by the $p$-series test.  So the endpoint $x=3$ is *not* included in our interval.

- When $x=-3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{n}}{{3}^{n}\sqrt{n}} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-3)^{n}}{{3}^{n}\sqrt{n}} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}}{\sqrt{n}} \\  & =-1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{4}}+⋯\,,\end{aligned}
$$

which is convergent by the alternating series test.  So the endpoint $x=-3$ *is* included in our interval.

Therefore, the interval of convergence is $[-3,3).$
